column1: # Measured pairs against the WCAG floor. NOT decoration: this is the
# accessibility floor, and a palette that drops below it is reported by
# hooks/08 rather than discovered by somebody who cannot read the site.
# `min` is 4.5 for body text and 3.0 for large text and UI edges.
# Re-measure when a colour changes. A stale row here is worse than no row,
# because it reads as a check that passed.
# WHICH THEME ARE THESE? eos / eos-light, re-measured 2026-08-05 against the
# canonical rows at blob 003fb9c. Named because it was NOT named before, and
# that is the deeper defect in this file:
# WARNING THIS TABLE IS THEME-BLIND. The rows are keyed `dark` and `light` as
# though the engine had one of each. It can render twenty. Any number here is a
# claim about ONE palette wearing the label of a whole scheme, so the moment an
# instance points at a different theme these rows are quietly about somebody
# else's colours. The real fix is deriving this at build time from the RESOLVED
# theme -- the same move that fixed section 1 of the token audit page -- and it is
# a piece of work, not a line. Flagged, not done.
# WHICH GROUND IS "surface"? The aliases resolve `surface` -> canonical `bg`
# and `surface-raised` -> `surface-1`, and every ground this engine actually
# PAINTS is one of those two: the table body, the sticky header, the hover row,
# the router panel, the section band.
# WARNING AND `surface-3` JOINED THEM ON 2026-08-05. It is the admonition
# background now, so a link or a marker inside a `!!! note` sits on the
# raised-most panel rather than on the page. That is why the `on callout` rows
# exist: the tightest ground on the site used to be untested because nothing
# painted it.
# WHAT THIS TABLE MISSED UNTIL NOW, which is worth more than any single number:
# it covered FOUR pairs while the engine paints eight things with a canonical
# token. accent-2, warn and on-accent were all being rendered and none was
# measured. A gate that covers half of what renders is not a gate, so the rows
# below were added with the palette rather than after somebody noticed.
# THE `warn on its own chip` ROWS ARE THE ONES TO KEEP. `warn` paints the
# `confidence` marker class, whose shape is `box` -- the chip draws the text in
# the colour ON A 10% WASH OF THE SAME COLOUR, so the marker fights its own
# background and the page ground is the WRONG thing to measure it against.
# Three amber candidates cleared the page and failed the chip.
# RED AND THE `rule on surface` ROWS WERE NEVER TRUE, NOT MERELY STALE. They
# recorded 3.2 dark and 3.1 light against a 3.0 floor; the real values are 2.34
# and 1.56. A sweep of all 19 dark palettes in maw-themes says ZERO of them
# clear 3.0 on a border, median 2.10 -- so this row has been certifying a bar
# that NOTHING in the design system meets, and passing, for as long as it has
# existed. Same shape as the accent/on-accent pair fixed this morning: a check
# whose subject does not exist cannot fail.
# They are left FAILING on purpose. Loosening `min` to make the report quiet
# would be choosing the number that suits the moment; whether a 3.0 hairline is
# the right target for a documentation site is Michael's call, and a loud honest
# failure is how it reaches him.
# WARNING ONE ROW HERE IS NOT A PASS/FAIL AND IS RECORDED ANYWAY: `link vs
# accent`, at 1.04 dark and 1.02 light with `min` 0.
# `link` was split out of `accent` on 2026-08-05 so a hyperlink would stop
# sharing a token with the note callout, the active nav row and the sticky
# column. The two colours are deliberately LEVEL in luminance -- subtler must not
# mean harder to see -- and separated by 106 degrees of HUE instead.
# Which means a reader with red-green or blue-yellow deficiency may not
# distinguish them. There is no floor to hold that to, so `min` is 0 and the
# number is here to be READ rather than gated: `accent` never letters body prose,
# so inside a paragraph the only coloured text is a link and it carries 7.31
# against the page. The thin case is `.dr-term`, which is coloured prose that is
# NOT clickable, and the fix for that is underlining real links.
